route.title: Contact identity, positive arithmetic orbits, and quadratic subdivision
route.mathematicalIdea: Follow proof.md in full: contact at x=f(t) yields f(f(t))=2f(t)-t. Positive forward iterates force f(t)>=t. The lower inequality at x=f(u) gives a quadratic displacement bound. Equal subdivision of a positive compact interval proves f(t)-t is constant. Verify both inequalities for f(t)=t+c, c>=0.
orderedMilestones: Use both inequalities at the contact point to prove the composition identity.
Prove all iterates positive and arithmetic, then use the Archimedean property to show f(t)>=t.
Derive both directions of the quadratic displacement comparison with explicit sign conditions.
Sum along equal subdivisions and let the integer subdivision size be arbitrarily large to prove constancy without assuming regularity.
Choose c=f(1)-1 and verify sufficiency using the arithmetic-geometric and root-mean-square inequalities.
assumptionsUsed: Exactly IsAdmissible f on PositiveReal -> PositiveReal; no continuity or monotonicity assumptions.
mathematicalRisks: Keep subtype coercions and positivity explicit.
Squaring needs nonnegative sides; divisions need positive denominators.
Do not assume the displacement is constant or weaken the bidirectional classification.

entries.collectionRationale: The supplied detailed mathematical proof replaces initial route generation only. All Lean evidence, DAG and proof gates remain active.
